title: Pakistan Hockey's Stunning Collapse: From 4 World Cups to 16 Straight Losses
excerpt: Once the most successful team in Hockey World Cup history, Pakistan finished their first FIH Pro League campaign without a single win — losing all 16 matches and conceding 79 goals.
body:
• Pakistan lost all 16 matches in their debut FIH Pro League 2025-26 season, scoring 22 goals while conceding 79 — the worst record in the league
  • The campaign ended with a 7-0 thrashing by England, prompting captain Ammad Shakeel Butt to publicly apologize to the nation
  • A four-time World Cup champion (1971, 1978, 1982, 1994) and three-time Olympic gold medalist, Pakistan has failed to qualify for the last three Olympics
  • The PHF has appointed Abu Bakar as new captain ahead of the 2026 Hockey World Cup in Belgium and the Netherlands

Pakistan's first-ever FIH Pro League campaign ended the way it began — with a loss. But the scale of the failure would have been unimaginable to those who watched the green shirts lift four World Cup trophies between 1971 and 1994.

The team finished their debut season without a single victory, losing all 16 matches across the 2025-26 campaign. The final indignity came on June 27: a 7-0 thrashing at the hands of England at London's Lee Valley Hockey and Tennis Centre, according to Centreline.

A Record of Futility

The numbers are grim. Pakistan scored 22 goals and conceded 79, finishing with a goal difference of minus 57 — the worst in the nine-team league. They lost twice to each of the other eight teams: Netherlands (5-2, 7-3), Argentina (3-2, 5-1), Australia (3-2, 3-0), Germany (5-2, 6-1), Spain (5-1), Belgium, India and England.

Captain Ammad Shakeel Butt posted a lengthy apology on social media. "Sleeping with the burden of defeat is not easy," he wrote, urging the federation and government to provide better facilities and preparation, according to Lord Media.

Pakistan had entered the Pro League only because New Zealand withdrew due to financial constraints. Players told Telecom Asia Sport they were frustrated by the lack of preparation — no camp, no international coach, and no plan for matches against top-ranked teams, IANS reported.

How a Hockey Superpower Fell

Pakistan's hockey heritage is one of the sport's greatest. Three Olympic gold medals (1960, 1968, 1984). Four World Cup titles — a record. Legends like Shahbaz Ahmed, Hassan Sardar and Samiullah Khan defined an era of attacking brilliance.

"The passion of hockey is not there anymore in the whole of Pakistan. There are few areas left where hockey is played."

— Shahbaz Ahmed Sr., captain of 1994 World Cup-winning team

The decline has roots in multiple failures. The transition from grass to synthetic turf in the late 1990s caught Pakistan flat-footed — one artificial pitch costs around $500,000, and the cash-strapped Pakistan Hockey Federation (PHF) could not provide them, according to Youlin Magazine. The PHF operates on an annual budget of just 4 million PKR while a single international tour costs 30 million PKR, PHF President Tariq Hussain Bugti told Al Jazeera.

Political interference, corruption and leadership battles within the PHF have compounded the problem. As recently as 2024, two rival groups each claimed to be the "real PHF" and threatened to send competing teams to the Sultan Azlan Shah Cup, according to Youlin Magazine. The collapse of departmental hockey — once the backbone of domestic competition — has eroded the grassroots pipeline.

India Angle: Rivalry Fading

For India's hockey community, Pakistan's decline removes one of the sport's great rivalries. India's own recovery — culminating in the 2021 Olympic bronze after a 41-year medal drought — stands in stark contrast. Pakistan last beat India in 2016 at the SAF Games. The two teams met in the Pro League in June, with India's superiority no longer in question.

What's Next

The PHF has appointed Abu Bakar as new captain, replacing Butt, on the recommendation of a committee featuring legends Islahuddin Siddiqui and Hassan Sardar, according to WE News. Pakistan qualified for the 2026 Hockey World Cup — co-hosted by Belgium and the Netherlands from August 14-30 — with a dramatic 4-3 win over Japan in March. It's a chance at redemption, but the Pro League results suggest the gap with the world's best remains enormous.
nri_angle: For India's hockey community, Pakistan's decline removes one of the sport's greatest rivalries and highlights India's own recovery trajectory.
